lessons: Keep the harness design: the single-envelope fixtures, _FixtureEffect with fixture-keyed stems, the pre-call budget, the per-journal run_seq and the closed schemas. All checks passed. Review snagged only on fixture realism and one budget-accounting bug.

Replace the shared template ticket body in every fixture. Write a real Goal, Scope fence and Acceptance criteria that the harvest judges. Each reject ticket must contain the impossible criterion. Each split ticket must list its multi-subsystem goals.

Make each fixture's scope fence cover every path in its harvest diff_stat. Allow an out-of-fence path only in oversight-scope-escape, where scope escape is the planted defect. Otherwise a diagnoser can fairly answer retry to the escalate and split fixtures.

The escalate rationales claim repeated attempts, but every harvest has run_seq 1. Either set run_seq > 1 and put prior findings in the spool_tails, or remove the claim of repetition from the rationale.

oversight-inverted-guard's run_record says premise_failed, which points to reject. Rewrite it to match the harvest: outcome gate_failed or ok, with a note consistent with a local inverted-condition oversight.

eval/diagnose.py ~l.377: when BudgetRefused fires on a re-prompt (call_seq 2), the break skips score() and drops that fixture's paid first call from summary.usd. Take the stopped total from budget.spent plus replayed costs. Add a test where the cap is crossed on a re-prompt.
Check each fixture as the model would see it: ticket, harvest and run_record should together point only to the expected verdict. Keep compact single-line JSON so the diff stays within 30 files.
reason: Review found concrete, fixable defects in the fixture content and one budget-summary accounting bug. The harness design and all mechanical gates passed, so the same capability can fix them with these findings.
